Critics have debated which of these games should be classified as the best-selling video game, mainly due to definitional disputes surrounding ''Tetris''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/minecraft-has-sold-176-million-copies-may-be-the-best-selling-game-ever/ |title=''Minecraft'' has sold 176 million copies, may be the best-selling game ever |first=Jody |last=Macgregor |website=[[PC Gamer]] |date=May 19, 2019 |access-date=November 8, 2019 |archive-date=August 16, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250816200135/https://www.pcgamer.com/minecraft-has-sold-176-million-copies-may-be-the-best-selling-game-ever/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="thebbc" /><ref name="gwr" />}}

This is a list of the best-selling [[video games]] worldwide, ranked up to 50th place by reported [[software]] unit sales. Reliable sources are split as to whether the title of best-selling video game should belong to ''[[Tetris]]'', a 1988 multi-platform [[puzzle video game]] created by [[Alexey Pajitnov]], or to ''[[Minecraft]]'', a 2011 multi-platform [[sandbox game]] created by [[Markus Persson]] and developed by [[Mojang Studios]]. Some sources consider ''Tetris'' to be the best-selling video game by combining the sales of all of its different versions, totaling 520 million as of 2022, while others consider the best-selling video game to be ''Minecraft'', which has sold over 425 million copies as of 2026, rejecting the aggregation of each ''Tetris'' release.{{Efn|name=Dispute|''Tetris'' is considered the best-selling video game by ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'',<ref>{{Cite news |title=''Minecraft'' {{!}} Popularity, Game Modes, & Creator |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Minecraft-electronic-game The best-selling single-platform game is ''[[Wii Sports]]'', with nearly 83&nbsp;million sales for the [[Wii]] console.{{Efn|name=WiiSports}}

==Criteria==
The 1998 game ''[[Snake (1998 video game)|Snake]]'' is estimated to have shipped on over 400&nbsp;million devices,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pocketgamer.biz/a-brief-history-of-mobile-games-in-the-beginning-there-was-snake/ |title=A Brief History of Mobile Games: In the beginning, there was Snake |first=Chris |last=Wright |website=[[Pocket Gamer]] |date=March 14, 2016 |access-date=April 26, 2025 |archive-date=June 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240628210958/https://www.pocketgamer.biz/a-brief-history-of-mobile-games-in-the-beginning-there-was-snake/ |url-status=live}}</ref> but is not listed as it was preinstalled and freely accessible on [[Nokia]] mobile phones.

For this list, standard re-releases, [[remaster#Video games|remasters]] and enhanced versions of games are considered iterative updates to the original, thus their sales are combined. In contrast, [[video game remake|remakes]] generally contain significant deviations from the original and are considered separate products.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.techradar.com/news/game-remakes-vs-remasters-whats-the-difference |title=Game remakes vs remasters: what's the difference? |first=Phil |last=Hayton |website=[[TechRadar]] |date=January 24, 2020 |access-date=May 10, 2025 |archive-date=January 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125165741/https://www.techradar.com/news/game-remakes-vs-remasters-whats-the-difference |url-status=live}}</ref> Likewise, [[expansion pack]]s are not combined with the base game to avoid inflating sales figures. Additionally, titles with unique release structures are classified based on their specific publishing context. Other metrics, such as "players" or "installs", typically refer to active users engaging with the game rather than sales, thus are not listed; even for paid games, these metrics could include free trials or other free promotions and cannot reliably be substituted for sales figures.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamekult.com/actualite/34-millions-de-pirates-pour-assassin-s-creed-iv-blag-flag-3050856813.html |title=34 millions de pirates pour Assassin's Creed IV : Black Flag |author=Kyujilo |website=Gamekult |language=French |date=October 30, 2023 |access-date=April 26, 2025 |archive-date=October 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030183102/https://www.gamekult.com/actualite/34-millions-de-pirates-pour-assassin-s-creed-iv-blag-flag-3050856813.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamereactor.eu/dead-by-daylight-hits-mega-60-million-players-milestone-1332753/ |title=Dead by Daylight hits mega 60 million players milestone |first=Ben |last=Lyons |website=[[Gamereactor]] |date=November 29, 2023 |access-date=April 26, 2025 |archive-date=November 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129203717/https://www.gamereactor.eu/dead-by-daylight-hits-mega-60-million-players-milestone-1332753/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Paid bundled titles are also included in this list; their sales often benefit from being packaged with other products, typically at a discounted price.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/the-pros-and-cons-of-the-bundle-promotion |title=The Pros and Cons of the Bundle Promotion |website=[[Game Developer (website)|Game Developer]] |first=Ulyana |last=Chernyak |date=November 3, 2014 |access-date=November 11, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210827202619/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/the-pros-and-cons-of-the-bundle-promotion |archive-date=August 27, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==List of best-selling games==

The listed developers and publishers correspond to each game's original release, and release years refer only to the first full public launch, excluding any prerelease stages. Rankings serve solely for numbering purposes and are not meant to be precise, reflecting the list's limited scope because there is no credible, comprehensive sales-tracking source for the video game industry,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/games/2024/apr/03/pushing-buttons-video-game-console-sales |title=Pushing Buttons: When we don't know the true sales figures for consoles, players lose out |first=Keza |last=MacDonald |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=April 3, 2024 |access-date=November 1, 2025 |archive-date=April 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240403164334/https://www.theguardian.com/games/2024/apr/03/pushing-buttons-video-game-console-sales |url-status=live}}</ref> unlike for [[list of highest-grossing films|films]], which have box office tracking sites such as ''[[Box Office Mojo]]'' and ''[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]''. Tied ranks are resolved using the [[Ranking#Standard competition ranking ("1224" ranking)|standard competition ranking]] method, in which entries with equal figures share the same rank and following ranks are increased based on the number of tied entries.
